aiModels.name: Soil nutrient prediction (geospatial feature engineering)
aiModels.shortDescription: Feature-rich geospatial pipeline (1,000+ engineered features) + soil-depth matching to predict multiple nutrients from satellite/climate/soil signals.
aiModels.fullDescription: Soil-nutrient prediction solution (Rhea challenge) built around heavy feature engineering and domain knowledge. Key elements: (1) 1,000+ features derived from satellite, climate and soil datasets, (2) soil-depth matching to align observations and improve signal consistency, and (3) multi-target regression to estimate several nutrient values at unsampled points. Intended for scalable nutrient mapping to guide fertiliser recommendations and soil-health interventions.
aiModels.useCase: Estimate multiple soil nutrients from geospatial + soil data at locations without lab tests.
aiModels.technicalRequirements: Uses open-source tools; may incorporate earth observation + climate datasets; must include preprocessing + download scripts for any external data.

aiModels.name: Soil nutrient prediction (domain-aware ensemble)
aiModels.shortDescription: Domain-aware ensemble that blends Random Forest + LightGBM, with adversarial feature selection; separate inference path for historical vs 2025 data.
aiModels.fullDescription: Soil-nutrient prediction solution (Rhea challenge) designed for robust generalisation across locations. Key elements: (1) domain-aware ensemble combining Random Forest and LightGBM, (2) adversarial feature-selection strategy to reduce spurious predictors, and (3) a split inference pipeline handling historical vs 2025 data differently to mitigate distribution shift. Outputs: multi-target regression for several soil nutrients, enabling nutrient mapping where lab tests are unavailable.
aiModels.useCase: Estimate multiple soil nutrients from geospatial + soil data at locations without lab tests.
aiModels.technicalRequirements: Uses open-source tools; may incorporate earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-2, Landsat) and climate datasets; must include preprocessing + download scripts for external data if used.

aiModels.name: Soil nutrient prediction (climate-zone & village models)
aiModels.shortDescription: Climate-zone + village-level modelling: Köppen–Geiger clustering, hierarchical statistics, and an ensemble to improve nutrient estimates without lab tests.
aiModels.fullDescription: Soil-nutrient prediction solution (Rhea challenge) emphasizing spatial generalisation. Approach: (1) clusters samples by climate similarity using Köppen–Geiger zones, (2) builds village-level models with hierarchical statistics to capture local patterns, and (3) combines diverse learners in an ensemble for stable multi-nutrient regression. Designed to support tailored soil recommendations where laboratory analysis is limited.
aiModels.useCase: Estimate multiple soil nutrients from geospatial + soil data at locations without lab tests.
aiModels.technicalRequirements: Uses open-source tools; may incorporate earth observation + climate datasets; must include preprocessing + download scripts for any external data.

aiModels.name: Produce recommendations (baseline/shared solution)
aiModels.shortDescription: Baseline/shared recommender system solution for the Farm to Feed online challenge (Zindi).
aiModels.fullDescription: Baseline/shared solution produced for the AI4SU online hackathon “Produce Recommendation Systems for Food Waste Reduction” (Farm to Feed, hosted on Zindi). The goal is to build a recommender system using anonymised transaction data to (1) predict purchase likelihood in the next 7 and 14 days and (2) estimate expected quantities per customer and SKU. This supports more relevant recommendations, better inventory and marketing decisions, and ultimately helps reduce food waste while improving access to fresh produce markets.
aiModels.useCase: Recommend fresh produce to customers by predicting which items they are likely to purchase in the next 7 and 14 days, and estimating expected quantities—helping reduce food waste and improve e-commerce operations for Farm to Feed.
aiModels.technicalRequirements: Recommender system / next-basket prediction in Python (pandas/numpy, scikit-learn + optional implicit/LightFM or gradient boosting). Must output purchase likelihood for 7/14 days and quantities per customer/SKU; includes transaction preprocessing, feature engineering, and reproducible inference scripts. Dependency file + run instructions.

studies.title: Unlocking the Data Ecosystem for African AgTech Startups
studies.description: This report maps the data and AI-driven agritech ecosystem across eight African countries, analysing key actors, funding dynamics, and policy environments. It highlights structural barriers to data access and proposes a roadmap to strengthen data ecosystems and enable AI innovation.
keyFindings: Agritech innovation is growing, but relies on small, fragmented, and localised datasets that limit scalability
Access to large, structured datasets (soil, weather, market data) remains a major bottleneck
Data collection, storage, and processing costs are high and constrain startup growth
Data ecosystems are fragmented, with limited incentives for public and private actors to share data
Talent shortages and weak pipelines contribute to a lack of data and AI expertise

studies.title: Data & Regulatory Landscape Report
studies.description: This report analyses the data governance, regulatory challenges, and AI adoption barriers faced by startups across agritech, climate, energy, and food sectors in eight African countries. It is based on survey data (39 startups) and qualitative interviews, providing actionable insights to support data-driven innovation.
keyFindings: Data is mission-critical for startups, yet access remains severely constrained due to poor data quality and unclear licensing
AI adoption is growing, but limited by infrastructure costs, talent gaps, and technical constraints
Data protection laws are generally seen as enabling, but compliance and internal governance remain complex
Data sharing is already widespread but lacks proper governance frameworks, creating trust and security risks
The biggest gap is the mismatch between active data sharing and insufficient governance infrastructure

studies.title: Policy Brief: Data without border event
studies.description: This policy brief synthesizes insights from multi-stakeholder workshops held in Abidjan, bringing together startups, policymakers, and ecosystem actors. It identifies key barriers to data access and proposes concrete policy recommendations to enable AI innovation in Africa.
keyFindings: Lack of access to high-quality, structured data is the main barrier to AI startup growth
Without data, startups cannot build credible AI products or attract investment
Data ecosystems remain fragmented, with limited sharing between public and private actors
Strong need for incentives and frameworks to encourage data sharing (e.g. funding tied to openness)
Trust, standardisation, and governance mechanisms are essential to unlock data collaboration

studies.title: AI & Data Use Cases in African Agritech
studies.description: This report compiles key AI and data-driven use cases identified throughout the AI4Startups programme in the African agritech sector. It highlights practical applications of AI to address agricultural challenges and improve productivity, resilience, and sustainability.

finalReport.title: AI4Startups – Hackathon Report: Challenges & Solutions
finalReport.description: This report presents the challenges addressed during the AI4Startups hackathons and showcases the solutions developed by participating startups. It highlights key insights from the experimentation phase and illustrates how data-driven innovation can address real-world problems.
